china-1923:p0784_1.rationale: Monthly pension amounts paid to the Imperial Family and banners, listed as part of the budget; pensions are public expenditure items.

china-1923:p0784_2.rationale: Surplus of maritime and native customs revenue for 1921, in taels, with a note on carry-forward to meet national loan obligations.

china-1923:p0784_3.rationale: Salt surplus released, salt revenue detained by provinces, and special items paid from the surplus; this is salt revenue as a fiscal matter.

china-1923:p0785_1.rationale: Peking Octroi collections against monthly expenses and earmarked funds (treasury notes, schools, judicial reform, students in Japan); this is a local revenue and expenditure account.
review_questions: Is a tag for local or municipal levies such as the octroi needed? The vocabulary has none.

china-1923:p0785_2.rationale: Amounts of mining, stamp, wine and tobacco, income and other taxes actually received by the Central Government.

china-1923:p0786_1.rationale: Summary of domestic and foreign government debts, secured and unsecured, with totals.

china-1923:p0789_1.rationale: Statement of secured domestic government loans with amounts issued and outstanding at the end of September 1922.

china-1923:p0791_1.rationale: Secured foreign debts with amounts borrowed and outstanding, interest rates and loan periods; the rows include Boxer Indemnity obligations.

china-1923:p0793_1.rationale: Deferred debts to German and Austrian creditors, with amounts, interest and security. The amounts are quantitative, so this is not a text table.

china-1923:p0793_2.rationale: Totals of the deferred German debts by place and currency, with an approximate dollar total.
